input: It is also worth noting that the two groups whose results are discussed here report pressure drop values for the benchmark material that are in clear conflict with one another, and this disagreement cannot simply be brushed aside. On closer inspection, however, it becomes apparent that the conditions under which the two sets of measurements were obtained were by no means identical. In one case, the pressure drop was measured across a bed that had been freshly packed for each test, so that the reported values relate to the bed of the benchmark material itself, whereas in the other case the reported pressure drop was taken across the assembled contactor as a whole, meaning that the fittings and end sections through which the gas enters and leaves are also included within the figure. It should also be said that neither group appears to have been careless in its work, since each set of results is thoroughly consistent within itself, and the disagreement only emerges when the two sets are placed side by side. Given this difference, it is perhaps unsurprising that the second set of values sits consistently above the first. Taking these considerations into account, there is a reasonable case for preferring the first set of values when the purpose in hand is the design of a packed bed, although this preference clearly depends on the configuration to which the values are going to be applied.
target: Against that reading, the conflict in the reported pressure drop values for the benchmark material follows the test conditions rather than the material. Within its own runs each group reproduces its values closely, and the disagreement lives between the groups rather than inside either set of measurements. Neither set of values carries an obvious measurement fault; the two sets differ because the quantity measured was not the same quantity. One group packed a fresh bed for each test and took the pressure drop across the bed alone, so its values belong to the benchmark material in packed form. The other group took the pressure drop across the assembled contactor, and its values include the entry and exit fittings through which the gas passes before and after the bed. A drop measured over bed and fittings together stands above a drop measured over the bed alone, and the gap between the two reports has the size and the direction that difference in arrangement predicts. For design of a packed bed, the bed-only values are the safer basis: the fittings of a new design are the designer's own, and a figure that already contains another contactor's fittings cannot be separated after the fact. The preference is limited to that use. Where the contactor as assembled sets the pressure drop, the whole-contactor values are the relevant ones, and the bed-only set understates what the gas meets in service.
